security_frame.attacker: Caliptra runtime firmware executing at supervisor mode on the Caliptra microcontroller, able to write the SoC interface register that triggers a firmware-update reset and able to write the PCR vault control and clear registers over AHB.
security_frame.precondition: A PCR entry holds a boot measurement, and firmware has set that entry's PCR_CTRL.lock bit to protect the measurement from being cleared. The lock is the only mechanism that stands between the stored measurement and a software clear.
security_frame.input: An AHB write of PCR_CTRL[n].lock to set the lock, then a write of INTERNAL_FW_UPDATE_RESET.core_rst to trigger a microcontroller-only reset, then an AHB write of PCR_CTRL[n].clear.
security_frame.protected_asset: PCR entry contents: boot measurements that an attestation quote is computed over. An attacker who can zero a PCR entry and re-extend it with values of their choosing controls what the platform attests to.
security_frame.security_property: PCR lock stickiness. src/pcrvault/config/pcrvault.md:6 states that the lock bit is sticky and only resets on a powergood cycle. A firmware-update reset is not a powergood cycle, so a set lock must survive it.
security_frame.implemented_logic: src/pcrvault/rtl/pv_reg.rdl:30 declares the lock field as sw=rw; swwel=true; hw=r with resetsignal = core_only_rst_b. src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:176 connects that reset signal to the module's core_only_rst_b input, and src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:1226 connects that input to cptra_uc_rst_b, the microcontroller-only reset that a firmware-update reset asserts. src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:110-111 feeds the lock value back as the swwel write-enable-low for both the lock field and the clear field, so while the lock is set neither can be written by software. src/pcrvault/rtl/pv.sv:130 makes PCR_CTRL[entry].clear.value drive the entry data hwclr, so a clear write zeroes the entry. The PCR entry data itself is declared at src/pcrvault/rtl/pv_reg.rdl:22 with resetsignal = hard_reset_b, so the data survives the same reset that clears the lock protecting it.

security_feature_bypassed: PCR lock stickiness across a firmware-update reset. The lock is specified to survive everything short of a powergood cycle, but is implemented with the microcontroller-only reset as its reset signal, so a firmware-update reset that firmware itself can trigger clears every PCR lock while leaving the measurements in place and then clearable.
proof_goal: Determine whether a set PCR_CTRL.lock bit survives a core_only_rst_b assertion as src/pcrvault/config/pcrvault.md:6 requires, and if it does not, whether the resulting unlocked state lets software clear a PCR entry whose data survived the same reset.
minimum_attack_sequence: Runtime firmware, or an earlier stage, provisions a PCR entry with a measurement and sets that entry's PCR_CTRL.lock bit. From this point the specification says the measurement cannot be cleared until a powergood cycle.
Firmware confirms the protection is live: a write of PCR_CTRL.clear is rejected because the lock feeds swwel for the clear field.
Firmware writes INTERNAL_FW_UPDATE_RESET.core_rst, which the boot FSM turns into an assertion of cptra_uc_rst_b. This is a supported firmware operation, not a fault injection.
The reset de-asserts. The PCR entry data survived because it resets on hard_reset_b, but the lock bit did not because it resets on core_only_rst_b.
Firmware writes PCR_CTRL.clear, which is now accepted because swwel is no longer held, and the measurement is zeroed. Firmware may then extend the entry with values of its choosing.
expected_evidence: A single-DUT simulation of the pv module driving real AHB writes and reads, measuring: that a provisioned entry reads back its data; that setting PCR_CTRL.lock reads back as set; that with the lock set a write of PCR_CTRL.clear is suppressed and the entry data survives; the state of the lock bit and of the entry data after a core_only_rst_b pulse; and whether a clear write accepted after that pulse zeroes the entry.

A structural audit that reads the declared resetsignal of the lock field and of the entry data field, traces the module's core_only_rst_b input to the signal connected at the pv instantiation and that signal's driver, confirms that signal is asserted by a firmware-writable register rather than only by an external reset pin, and collects the in-tree statements on PCR lock stickiness. The audit must also record the equivalent KeyVault declaration as an in-tree contrast, because the KeyVault lock fields carry the same resetsignal and their in-tree table states a different stickiness requirement.
success_criteria: The claim is upheld only if BOTH the simulation shows a set lock cleared by a core_only_rst_b pulse while the entry data survives the same pulse AND a clear write that was suppressed before the pulse is accepted after it and zeroes the entry, AND the audit shows core_only_rst_b at this instantiation is reachable from a firmware-writable register rather than only from an external pin.
If the lock survives the core_only_rst_b pulse, the claim is withdrawn: the declared resetsignal would then not have the effect the reading of the register description suggests.

If the lock clears but the entry data clears with it, the claim is withdrawn as a security finding and recorded as a reset-domain observation only, because a cleared entry holds no measurement to protect.

If the lock clears and the data survives, but the post-reset clear write is still suppressed by some other mechanism, the claim is downgraded to an integrity-of-lock-state finding and the absence of a data-clearing path is recorded explicitly rather than glossed.

Pre-committed scope limit: this case does not claim that core_only_rst_b is the wrong reset signal for the KeyVault lock fields. The KeyVault in-tree table at docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:2459-2460 names core_only_rst_b in its reset column, so the KeyVault declaration matches at least one of its own in-tree statements. The PCR vault has no such table column, only the prose stickiness sentence, and it is that sentence this case tests.
non_findings_intent: Suspected but unproven at plan time: that the same reset-domain mismatch is exploitable on the KeyVault lock fields. To be excluded from the verdict, because the KeyVault carries its own in-tree reset column naming core_only_rst_b and the resulting ambiguity is a specification question already recorded separately, not a defect this case can decide.

Suspected but unproven at plan time: that a PCR entry can be usefully re-extended with attacker-chosen values after being cleared. The single hardware write client for the PCR vault is the SHA-512 hash-extend path, which the module-boundary testbench can drive, but whether a complete quote-forging flow is reachable depends on the SHA-512 control sequence and is outside a pv module-boundary measurement. The case will claim the clear, and record re-extension as the consequence it does not itself measure.

To be measured without a pre-assigned verdict: whether PCR_CTRL.clear is a singlepulse field, and therefore whether the post-reset clear needs one write or a held value. This affects how the attack sequence is written but not whether it succeeds.
